expl.summary: This formula uses no jet-mass observable and no observable that equals (m/ΣpT)² in disguise: every if-statement tests angular widths (ΣzΔR, λ₁, λ₂, Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, e₂, e₃), subjet distances, N-subjettiness, particle pT shares and the total pT. Each of the 16 neurons is a clipped sum of such if-statements, each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others, and the formula reaches an accuracy of 0.654 on the validation jets. Mass information returns only indirectly, through λ₁+λ₂: the compactness neuron 13 falls with m/ΣpT (rank correlation -0.756), neuron 2 falls with jet mass (-0.729) and the q score falls with jet mass (-0.75), although none of these quantities is an input. The t score subtracts compactness (neuron 13, ΣzΔR < 0.148, -47%) and adds overall angular size (neuron 10, +26%), so it follows ΣzΔR, λ₁+λ₂ and λ₁ (rank correlations 0.91-0.92); it also subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the 5 hardest particles, -16%). Quarks and gluons sit highest on the narrow-jet neuron 9 (small λ₁ and λ₂), which feeds the q score (+56%) and the g score (+22%); the g score adds the collimated-core neuron 2 (+38%) and subtracts neuron 5 (-14%), on which quarks sit far above all other jets. W and Z jets sit high on the elongated two-prong neurons 7 and 11: neuron 7 feeds both boson scores (Z +35%, W +12%), neuron 11 only the W score (+24%). Both boson scores subtract the neurons for pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 with a large minor axis (neuron 3) and broad off-centre spread (neuron 6). Without a mass window, W and Z are separated by λ₁+λ₂ windows: neuron 14 (λ₁ between 0.0065 and 0.012, small soft-drop angle) and neuron 15 (ΣzΔR above 0.087 with λ₁ below 0.0164), on both of which Z jets sit highest, take 10% and 8% out of the W score, while neuron 14 adds 6% to the Z score.

0.title: compact, elongated jet with subjet axes 0.14-0.17 apart
0.measures: Pushed up for small e₃ (< 0.000512, its strongest term, share 0.115), for λ₁ < 0.0120 (0.107) and for a largest 3-subjet distance above 0.143 (0.069); pushed down for the very narrowest jets (λ₁ < 0.00418, -0.06; ΣzΔR < 0.0807, -0.045), for τ₂ < 0.0171 (-0.053), for an off-centre pT centroid (> 0.00679, -0.045) and for subjet axes spread further than 0.169 and 0.199 (-0.043, -0.033). It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (rank correlation 0.562) and falls with planar flow (-0.562), N₂ (-0.531) and τ₂₁ (-0.521). Mean values: W 1.93, Z 1.89, t 0.34, q 0.18, g 0.16; it is zero for 85.4% of gluons, 87.1% of quarks and 79.3% of tops, but only for 23.2% of W and 20.9% of Z jets.
0.role: It raises the W score (+9%) and lowers the g score (-6%). It does not enter the q, Z or t scores; the Z score, although Z jets sit almost as high on it as W jets, takes the related two-prong neuron 7 instead.

1.title: moderately wide, high-pT jet with pT shared beyond the hardest particles
1.measures: Pushed down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR < 0.102, its strongest term, -0.098; λ₁ < 0.00838 together with λ₂ < 0.00113, -0.069), for a soft particle 7 (z₇ < 0.0647 and < 0.0867, -0.067 and -0.05) and for subjet axes closer than 0.346 (-0.045); pushed up for λ₁ < 0.0120 (0.069), for high total pT (log of total pT > 6.38, 0.068) and for τ₁ < 0.103 (0.037). It rises with Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, ΣzΔR and λ₁ (rank correlations 0.572, 0.57, 0.568) and with jet mass (0.55), which is not an input. Mean values: t 1.24, Z 1.08, g 0.71, W 0.62, q 0.30; it is zero for 68.6% of quarks and 56.5% of gluons, 19.7% of tops.
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%), where it marks the difference between gluons and the quarks that sit lowest on it, and raises the Z score a little (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: collimated jet with many particles inside ΔR < 0.05
2.measures: Its strongest terms push it down when particle 7 carries more than 2.32% of the pT (z₇ > 0.0232, -0.166), when the total pT is high (log of total pT > 6.08, -0.116) and when Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.112 (-0.075); it is pushed up when particle 7 has pT > 20.1 GeV (0.101), and a linear pT_7 term and pT_7 < 53.4 GeV push it down (-0.049, -0.052). It falls with the largest subjet-pair mass (rank correlation -0.731) and with jet mass (-0.729), neither of which is an input, and rises with M₂ (0.668) and the number of particles within ΔR < 0.05 (0.595). Mean values: g 3.53, q 2.52, W 1.69, Z 1.36, t 1.22; it is non-zero for most jets of every type (zero for 4.5% of gluons, 23.9% of tops).
2.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+38%). It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores, even though quarks sit second-highest on it; quarks are pulled out of the g score by neuron 5.

3.title: pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 in jets with a large minor axis (λ₂)
3.measures: Switched off for a small minor axis: λ₂ < 0.00341 is by far its strongest term (-0.323). It is pushed up for two subjets more than 0.168 apart (0.078), ΣzΔR > 0.0666 (0.06), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.293 (0.058) and a largest 3-subjet distance above 0.213 (0.048), and pushed down again for ΣzΔR > 0.102 (-0.075) and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.326 (-0.043). It follows the pT share and the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlations 0.723 and 0.714). Mean values: t 3.44, g 0.81, q 0.39, Z 0.11, W 0.01; it is zero for 98.9% of W jets, 91.2% of quarks, 83% of Z jets and 82.2% of gluons, but only for 23.6% of tops.
3.role: It lowers the W score (-15%) and the Z score (-21%), and raises the t score slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: two close subjets (low N₂, τ₂₁) in jets that are not the narrowest
4.measures: Pushed up for a smallest 3-subjet distance below 0.209 (its strongest term, 0.132), small e₃ (< 0.000187, 0.107) and N₂ < 0.223 (0.04); pushed down for narrow jets (λ₁ < 0.00651, -0.106; λ₁ < 0.00838, -0.068) and for close subjets combined with a small minor axis (sj3 ΔR_min < 0.209 and λ₂ < 0.00341, -0.102). It falls with N₂, τ₂₁ and D₂ (β = 2) (rank correlations -0.669, -0.662, -0.646). Mean values: Z 2.33, t 1.67, W 1.41, g 0.47, q 0.23; it is zero for 89.5% of quarks and 82.2% of gluons, 35.9% of W and 27.2% of Z jets.
4.role: It raises the Z score (+4%) and the t score (+5%) and lowers the q score (-8%). It does not enter the g or W scores.

5.title: pT concentrated in the 5 hardest particles, low Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, moderate total pT
5.measures: Pushed down for total pT below 739.5 GeV (its strongest term, -0.091), for a centred pT centroid (< 0.0378, -0.055) and for a hardest particle within ΔR 0.0641 of the axis (-0.051); pushed up when the 5 hardest particles carry less than 579.9 GeV (0.079), for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ < 0.216 (0.069), for small e₂ together with small λ₂ (0.048) and for small e₃ (< 0.000187, 0.045). It rises with the pT of the 3 and 5 hardest particles (rank correlations 0.717, 0.71) and falls with z₇ (-0.723). Mean values: q 4.41, g 1.41, W 1.36, Z 1.35, t 0.50; it is zero for 11.5% of quarks and for 31-42% of the other jets.
5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14%) and the t score (-16%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.

6.title: broad, off-centre spread with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4
6.measures: Pushed down for jets whose farthest particle lies within ΔR 0.177 (its strongest term, -0.086), for a small minor axis (λ₂ < 0.00113, -0.084), for ΣzΔR > 0.0872 (-0.076) and for a largest 3-subjet distance above 0.0346 (-0.072); pushed up for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.252 (0.061), C₂ < 0.0358 (0.06), a largest 3-subjet distance above 0.179 (0.042) and λ₂ < 0.00341 (0.041). It follows the pT share at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation 0.503) and the centroid offset (0.502). Mean values: t 2.86, g 1.26, q 0.54, Z 0.39, W 0.08; it is zero for 93.6% of W jets and 85.5% of quarks, 27.7% of tops.
6.role: It raises the g score (+5%) and the q score (+9%) and lowers the W score (-10%) and the Z score (-15%). It does not enter the t score.

7.title: elongated two-prong jet of intermediate λ₁+λ₂, low D₂
7.measures: Built from λ₁+λ₂ windows rather than one dominant term: pushed down for λ₁ > 0.0164 (-0.061), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.347 (-0.059), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ < 0.424 (-0.057), ΣzΔR > 0.0872 (-0.05) and λ₁ < 0.00484 (-0.041), and pushed up for ΣzΔR > 0.102 (0.054), τ₁ < 0.0887 (0.046), ΣzΔR > 0.0479 together with D₂ < 2.36 (0.046), λ₁ < 0.00838 (0.043) and λ₁ > 0.00246 (0.039). It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (rank correlation 0.579) and falls with planar flow (-0.579), D₂ (β = 2) (-0.52) and τ₂₁ (-0.509). Mean values: Z 3.94, W 2.67, t 1.19, g 1.00, q 0.51; it is zero for 74.2% of quarks, 60.5% of tops and 52.9% of gluons, and for only 9.1% of W and 7.5% of Z jets.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+35%, its largest input) and the W score (+12%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

8.title: centred jet with all three subjet axes within 0.2
8.measures: Pushed down when the 3 subjet axes lie within 0.107 of each other (its strongest term, -0.123), partly restored when the 3 hardest particles also have ΣzΔR² < 0.0154 (0.079); pushed up for a very small minor axis (λ₂ < 0.000195, 0.054) and for subjet axes within 0.199 (0.049) and 0.143 (0.038). It falls with the centroid offset and λ₁+λ₂ (rank correlations -0.377, -0.344). Mean values: q 0.50, g 0.46, W 0.28, Z 0.10, t 0.07; it is zero for about half of quarks, gluons and W jets and for 92.2% of tops.
8.role: It lowers the W score slightly (-2%). It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores.

9.title: narrow jet (small λ₁ and λ₂), centred, total pT below 988 GeV
9.measures: Pushed up mainly for λ₁ < 0.00595 together with λ₂ < 0.00113 (its strongest term, 0.145), for total pT below 988.4 GeV (0.091), for τ₁ < 0.0437 with a centred pT centroid (0.051) and for subjet axes within 0.213 (0.039); pushed down for the very narrowest jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0408, -0.041; ΣzΔR < 0.0546, -0.038) and for total pT below 813.4 GeV (-0.04). It falls with λ₁, λ₁+λ₂ and ΣzΔR (rank correlations -0.708, -0.704, -0.693). Mean values: q 6.53, g 4.77, W 1.81, t 1.19, Z 1.02; it is zero for 11.6% of quarks and 21.5% of gluons, but for 60.7% of Z jets and 51.6% of tops.
9.role: It raises the q score (+56%, its largest input) and the g score (+22%), and lowers the W score (-3%) and the Z score (-4%). It does not enter the t score.

10.title: overall angular size: grows with λ₁, ΣzΔR above 0.148
10.measures: Its strongest term is linear in λ₁ (0.199); it is pushed down for ΣzΔR < 0.148 (-0.118), Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.197 (-0.076) and a linear e₂ term (-0.053), and pushed up for two subjets more than 0.129 apart (0.074, partly removed above 0.159, -0.066) and λ₂ > 0.000195 (0.048). It follows ΣzΔR, λ₁+λ₂ and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlations 0.862, 0.861, 0.852). Mean values: t 4.36, Z 1.95, W 1.88, g 1.08, q 0.49; it is zero for 65.8% of quarks and 37.4% of gluons, and almost never for tops (1.4%).
10.role: It raises the t score (+26%) and lowers the q score (-18%). It does not enter the g, W or Z scores.

11.title: compact, elongated jet of intermediate λ₁+λ₂ (λ₁ < 0.012, low planar flow)
11.measures: Pushed up mainly for λ₁ < 0.0120 (its strongest term, 0.168), for λ₁ < 0.0164 together with λ₂ < 0.00113 (0.075), for planar flow < 0.253 (0.071), τ₁ < 0.0728 (0.05) and two subjets more than 0.129 apart (0.039); pushed down for the narrowest jets (e₂ < 0.0445, -0.062; ΣzΔR < 0.0611 and < 0.0717, -0.052 and -0.05). It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (rank correlation 0.58) and falls with planar flow (-0.58), D₂ (β = 2) (-0.523) and τ₂₁ (-0.503). Mean values: W 4.05, Z 3.31, g 1.26, q 0.88, t 0.77; it is zero for 71.2% of tops, 37.5% of quarks and 23.4% of gluons, and for only 2.6% of W and 3.8% of Z jets.
11.role: It raises the W score (+24%, its largest input). It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores.

12.title: very wide jet with many particles (ΣzΔR > 0.125)
12.measures: Almost always zero: it needs ΣzΔR > 0.125 (its strongest term, 0.282) and is pushed down for Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.386 (-0.125), for e₂ > 0.0634 (-0.068) and for a wide soft-drop angle (R_g > 0.325) at total pT below e^6.90 (-0.162, partly restored below e^6.70, 0.107). It follows the number of particles beyond ΔR 0.4 and the total particle count (rank correlations 0.821, 0.82). Mean values: t 0.30, g 0.09, q 0.03, W and Z 0.00; it is non-zero for 25.5% of tops and for almost no other jets.
12.role: It does not enter any of the five class scores, so it has almost no effect on the classification.

13.title: compactness: ΣzΔR below 0.148, λ₁ below 0.0164
13.measures: Dominated by ΣzΔR < 0.148 (share 0.33) and λ₁ < 0.0164 (0.114); it is pushed down when the compact ΣzΔR coincides with total pT below e^6.80 (-0.071), for C₂ (β = 2) < 0.00903 (-0.061), τ₁ < 0.114 (-0.058) and e₂ < 0.0800 (-0.048).
